title: How to read a day's work
content:
Call the working_day_window function for the exact window this run covers, then read what happened inside it across the configured repositories: commits you pushed, pull requests you opened, merged or closed, reviews you submitted, and issues you closed or commented on decisively.

Group by outcome, never by repository and never by event. Six commits that fix one bug are one item. A pull request opened in the morning and merged in the afternoon is one item about the change that shipped, not two about its lifecycle. Two repositories touched for the same feature are one item naming the feature.

For each item, decide which of three states it is in:

1. **Shipped** — merged, closed, released, or otherwise done and in the hands of whoever needed it.
2. **In progress** — real work happened and it is not done. Say what is left, not what was done.
3. **Blocked** — it is waiting on a person, a review, an answer or a decision. Name who or what it waits on. Work that is merely unfinished is not blocked, and calling it blocked wastes the one section anybody acts on.

Reviews you gave are work: a review that unblocked someone else's change belongs under shipped, named as the change it unblocked. Honour 'include_reviews' from the WorkflowManager_get_installation_params tool (slug 'ship_log') when it is turned off.

Read 'repositories' from the same settings. A repository the connection cannot see is reported once, in a single line at the end, rather than dropped silently.

title: How to write the ship log
content:
Three sections, in this order and never reordered: Shipped, In progress, Blocked. Skip a section that is empty rather than writing "none" under it. A day where every section is empty is one line saying so — a quiet day reported as a quiet day keeps the message worth reading.

Each line is one sentence in the first person, past tense, naming the outcome rather than the mechanism: "fixed the retry loop that was dropping streamed tool calls", not "merged PR #412 in unifyai/unify (3 commits)". Link the pull request or issue at the end of the line; never make the link the sentence.

Do not report time spent, counts of commits, or lines changed. Nobody has ever acted on a line count, and a hard bug looks like nothing next to a rename.

Blocked lines name the person or decision and what unblocks it, so tomorrow starts from them.

Where to send it comes from 'post_to' in the WorkflowManager_get_installation_params tool (slug 'ship_log'): post there when it names a channel, and deliver as a chat message when it is empty. Post the same text either way — a log written to be read by a team is the right log for the person who did the work too.
